entry.label: Regulation
entry.description: The constraint of possible outcomes under disturbance in relation to specified goals, essential variables or acceptable states. Regulation can use feedback, feedforward, structure, constraint or combinations of them.
entry.canonical_definition: A relation among disturbances, a reguland, a regulator and acceptable outcomes in which outcome variety is constrained relative to a stated goal or essential-variable range.

profile.title: Regulation
profile.canonical_definition: A relation among disturbances, a reguland, a regulator and acceptable outcomes in which outcome variety is constrained relative to a stated goal or essential-variable range.
profile.summary: Regulation is the work of keeping outcomes within acceptable ranges despite disturbance. It may operate through feedback, anticipation, constraints, buffering, redundancy, local autonomy or changes to the environment.
profile.why_it_matters: Regulation is often collapsed into command and control. Ashby instead asks what variety of disturbance reaches the system, what responses are available and which outcomes count as acceptable. The regulator may be distributed rather than a boss or central unit.
key_distinctions: acceptable range vs one fixed target
historical_lineage: physiological regulation and governor analysis predate cybernetics
Ashby formalised regulation in terms of variety and outcomes
practice_connections: identify the variable that must remain viable
map disturbance variety before adding controls
ask where regulatory intelligence already sits
protect local discretion where it carries necessary variety
open_checks: legal and institutional regulation as a distinct lineage
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.
